# Critique — Pattern 10 (Demographics & Context)

The slot allocation across the 255 slots was distributed as follows: Age & Life-Stage (~10%), Living Situation (~15%), Geography & Economic Context (~25%), Access, Education, Disability, & Social Connection (~25%), and self-monitoring/lifestyle fillers (~25%). We chose Approach A (exclude entirely) for sensitive demographics like race, ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, and immigration status because these variables are better captured in user-managed application profiles and carry significant discrimination risks in a portable bit field. Reaching exactly 255 questions felt highly forced; many self-monitoring and general habit questions (positions 245–255) served as filler. Overlaps exist with the Mental Health and Environmental domains (e.g., social isolation, rural/urban settings) as housing location and social connection directly impact psychiatric status. The V-flag was systematically set to `true` on questions representing positive social factors, health insurance coverage, and higher educational access to align with a convention where a stored bit `1` reflects risk or socioeconomic barriers. We paraphrased CMS's AHC Health-Related Social Needs and PRAPARE concepts to keep the phrasing lay-friendly. The weakest question is position 253 ("Do you log your demographic symptoms weekly...") as it is a generic template fallback that makes little semantic sense for demographics, highlighting the constraints of the 255-question requirement.
